ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a partial Routh table. The left-side row labels are s^3 and s^2; the two coefficients in the s^3 row are 1 and (2K+3), and the two coefficients in the s^2 row are 2K and 4. Reasoning: Continue filling in according to the Routh table of a third-order system, the first-column element of the s^1 row is ((2K)(2K+3)-1·4)/(2K). The first-column element of the s^0 row is 4. Stability requires all elements in the first column of the Routh table to be positive, therefore 1>0, 2K>0, ((2K)(2K+3)-4)/(2K)>0, and 4>0 are needed. From 2K>0 obtain K>0. Under the condition K>0, the denominator 2K is positive, so (2K)(2K+3)-4>0 is also needed, that is, 4K^2+6K-4>0. Factoring gives 4K^2+6K-4 = 2(2K-1)(K+2), so 2(2K-1)(K+2)>0. Combining with K+2>0 when K>0, therefore 2K-1>0 must hold, that is, K>1/2. Therefore the stability range is 0.5<K<∞.
